title: Three Drugs Together Cleared HIV Where None Could Alone
hook: In newborn primates treated within three days of exposure, a one-time combination of three therapies completely cleared the virus — something none of the three achieved on its own.
key_points: Regimen combined standard antiretrovirals, broadly neutralizing antibodies, and leronlimab.
Given to newborn nonhuman primates within three days of exposure.
The combination completely cleared the virus; no single component did.
Leronlimab is experimental — it blocks a receptor HIV uses to enter cells.
Animal study, and the tight three-day window is a major practical constraint.
content_html: HIV is famously hard to eliminate: it embeds itself in the body's cells and waits, which is why treatment is lifelong rather than curative. Researchers report that in newborn nonhuman primates, a one-time combination of three therapies given within three days of exposure completely cleared the virus.
extra_html:
The regimen paired standard antiretroviral drugs with broadly neutralizing antibodies and leronlimab, an experimental antibody. What makes the result notable is the arithmetic: none of the three cleared the virus on its own. Only together did they finish the job, which suggests each is closing a different escape route the others leave open.

The caveats are substantial and worth stating plainly. This is an animal study, in newborns, with a three-day treatment window — an extremely narrow one in practice, though it maps onto real scenarios like mother-to-child transmission at birth. Nothing here says anything about clearing established infection in adults. What it does offer is a proof of principle that combination approaches can achieve what single agents cannot, which is the direction cure research has been pointing for years.

flashcards.prompt: What was the key result of the three-part HIV regimen in newborn primates?

choices.text: It fully cleared the virus, though no single component could
Each of the three drugs cleared the virus equally well alone
It reduced symptoms but left viral levels unchanged

flashcards.explanation_html: The combination of antiretrovirals, broadly neutralizing antibodies, and leronlimab completely cleared the virus — an effect none of the three produced alone.

flashcards.prompt: What is the biggest practical limitation of this result?
flashcards.back_html: Treatment had to start within three days of exposure, in newborn nonhuman primates. Translating that timing and species to people is unproven.

flashcards.prompt: What are 'broadly neutralizing antibodies' doing in this regimen?
flashcards.back_html: They're one of the three components combined with standard antiretrovirals and the experimental antibody leronlimab — no one of which cleared the virus alone.
